intro: No SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 shift appears to have been held on 2 October, which was Gandhi Jayanti. Review videos and analysis pages move straight from the 1 October papers to the 5 October papers, and one reviewer said in a class on 2 October that there was no exam that day. A video posted on 3 October counts only five shifts so far, all from 30 September and 1 October. We did not find an SSC notice stating this, so the call rests on these reports. If you were allotted 2 October, check your admit card and the SSC website.

shifts.note: No paper was reported for the 10 AM slot on 2 October. No candidate reviews exist for this slot, and reviewers say there was no exam on this date. No SSC notice was found, so this is based on those reports. Videos titled '2 October' or '3 October' with full-day analysis are not reviews of a paper held on 2 October.

faqs.q: Was SSC CGL Tier 1 held on 2 October 2026?
faqs.a: It does not look like it. 2 October was Gandhi Jayanti, no shift reviews exist for the day, and reviewers describe the exam as having had no paper that day. We did not find an SSC notice, so check your admit card if you were allotted this date.

faqs.q: Which dates had SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 papers so far?
faqs.a: Papers were reported on 30 September (afternoon and evening slots), 1 October (three shifts) and 5 October (three shifts). The 10 AM slot on 30 September was not held at most centres.

faqs.q: Is there any shift analysis or good attempts figure for 2 October?
faqs.a: No. There was no paper to review, so there are no difficulty ratings or good attempts for this date. Any page claiming a '2 October' analysis is likely about another day.

faqs.q: What should I do if my admit card shows 2 October?
faqs.a: Check the SSC website and your login for the latest notice and your exact date and shift. Do not rely on coaching sites or videos for your personal schedule.

faqs.q: When did SSC CGL Tier 1 2026 papers resume after 1 October?
faqs.a: Reviews show the next papers on 5 October, in three shifts. See the 5 October analysis for those shifts. All figures there are unofficial.
